name: MariaDB (MariaDB plc / MariaDB Corporation and the MariaDB Foundation)
origin_detail: Forked from MySQL in 2009 (first release 5.1.38 on 2009-10-29) by Michael 'Monty' Widenius and other original MySQL developers, who feared Oracle's acquisition of Sun, MySQL's owner since 2008, would restrict MySQL. The company began in 2010 as SkySQL Corporation Ab (founders incl. Patrik Backman, Kaj Arnö and Widenius), merged with Monty Program Ab on 2013-04-23 and became MariaDB Corporation Ab on 2014-10-01. The nonprofit MariaDB Foundation (incorporated in Delaware) was announced in December 2012. Finnish roots; Wikipedia lists HQ as Silicon Valley and Dublin, Ireland.
openness_notes: MariaDB Server is GPLv2 (connectors LGPLv2.1) and the Foundation states it 'will remain Free and Open Source Software licensed under GPLv2'; with a nonprofit foundation the server project itself approaches level 4. The company authored the Business Source License (MaxScale 2.0.0-2.0.4 under BSL 1.0, later BSL 1.1) and sells enterprise tooling and cloud, so the company is open core (2).

license_history.note: Converts after at most four years to GPLv2-or-later; designed so other vendors can adopt it. Year of MaxScale 2.0 not confirmed in fetched pages.

relicensing_events.from: open source (prior MaxScale licence not confirmed)
relicensing_events.outcome_note: MariaDB created the BSL template that spread through this group: CockroachDB adopted 'MariaDB's Business Source License (BSL) 1.1' in 2019, Lightbend used BSL 1.1 for Akka in 2022 and HashiCorp BSL 1.1 in 2023.

exit_events.counterparty: Angel Pond Holdings Corp. (SPAC); NYSE: MRDB
exit_events.note: Announced February 2022, completed December 2022; renamed MariaDB plc. The share price then 'declined sharply'. Listing valuation not confirmed.
Tender offer for 100% of shares completed 2024-09-10; ~$37M per Wikipedia (the press release gives no value); Rohit de Souza became CEO; ~700 active customers.

risk_events: 2022-12: SPAC listing, followed by a sharp share-price decline
2023-10: SkySQL cloud service discontinued and staff laid off
2024-09: Taken private by K1 for about $37M
robustness: The code is robust independent of the company: GPLv2 server and a nonprofit foundation, which in 2025 signed an MoU recognising MariaDB plc as primary code contributor for 2022-2024. The company has been fragile (SPAC, collapse, ~$37M take-private) and under K1 is rebuilding by acquisition: Codership/Galera (May 2025), SkySQL back (announced 2025-08-26) and GridGain (March 2026, per Wikipedia).
openness_effect_assessment: MariaDB shows openness protecting the code but not the company. The GPL and the foundation let the community route around Oracle's control of MySQL, and MariaDB Server remains widely used. The commercial vehicle raised about $123M, listed by SPAC at the 2022 peak and sold for about $37M two years later.
key_takeaway: MariaDB exists because MySQL changed hands: it is a founder-led fork to keep the code under community control, backed by a nonprofit foundation. Its company struggled (SPAC listing, then a roughly $37M private-equity take-private) while the GPL server persists, separating the robustness of the code from that of the company. It also wrote the Business Source License used across the later relicensing wave.
